evals.prompt: Use $release to draft notes for v1.4.0 from v1.3.0; do not publish or edit the existing changelog.
evals.expected_output: Curated notes from v1.3.0..HEAD with a compare link and no repository or forge mutation.
assertions: The v1.3.0..HEAD commit and diff range is inspected
The notes are reader-focused and include a valid compare link
CHANGELOG.md is not edited
No tag is created or pushed and no forge release is created

evals.prompt: Use $release to draft the initial v1.0.0 release notes from this repository's root commit and later feature commits.
evals.expected_output: Initial-release notes based on the complete history, including the root commit and no compare link.
assertions: The complete history including the root commit is inspected
The response reports that no previous release tag exists
No compare link is included

evals.prompt: Use $release to prepare v2.0.0 and update the existing changelog for its breaking changes, but do not publish.
evals.expected_output: A changelog update in the established style with explicit breaking changes and no tag or release publication.
assertions: The existing changelog is updated in its established style
Breaking changes are clearly identified
No second changelog is created
No tag is created or pushed and no forge release is created

evals.prompt: Use $release to publish v1.5.0 from this clean GitHub Flow repository. HEAD matches the remote release commit and the tag does not exist.
evals.expected_output: A verified annotated tag and GitHub release created from the exact remote commit and read back successfully.
assertions: The tag's local and remote absence and the release commit are verified before mutation
An annotated tag is created and pushed
gh release create is run with --verify-tag and the release is read back
The response reports the verified release URL and tag
No existing tag is moved

evals.prompt: Use $release to publish v1.6.0, but the worktree currently has uncommitted plugin-version and changelog preparation changes.
evals.expected_output: Publication stops and directs the preparation changes through the configured commit and PR workflow.
assertions: Publication stops before creating a tag
The response directs preparation changes through commit and PR before retrying
No direct commit on main or tag of uncommitted content occurs

evals.prompt: Use $release to publish ship plugin version 5.2.0 from a repository whose .agents/ship.md requires bucket-scoped <plugin>@X.Y.Z release tags.
evals.expected_output: A ship-scoped release using tag ship@5.2.0, ship-only history, and a manifest and marketplace version check before publication.
assertions: The tag is ship@5.2.0 rather than repo-wide v5.2.0
The repository tag format in .agents/ship.md overrides the claude plugin tag default
The ship plugin.json version and its marketplace entry are confirmed to match the tag
Release history is limited to the ship plugin directory
Unrelated plugin changes are excluded from the release

evals.prompt: Make the SDK publish-ready for its first 0.1.0 release, but don't do npm releases for now. (The repository has no release tags; packages are versioned 0.0.0 and an npm publish workflow runs on tag push.)
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a prepare request: it updates the package versions and drafts initial release notes from the full history, but creates no tag, pushes nothing that triggers publication, runs no npm publish, and creates no forge release. It notes the preparation changes must go through commit and PR before any publication.
assertions: No git tag is created or pushed
npm publish is not run and no forge release is created
Release notes are drafted from the full history including the root commit, with no compare link
The response states that the preparation changes need the commit and PR workflow before publication

evals.prompt: Do release. (GitHub Flow repository; the last tag is v0.3.0, main has several feat and fix commits since, and package.json still says 0.3.0.)
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches tags, picks the next version from the commits since v0.3.0, and because package.json must change it routes the version bump through a commit and PR instead of tagging main directly. It tags and publishes only after the bump is merged and HEAD matches the remote release commit.
assertions: git fetch origin --tags runs before the version is chosen
The proposed version follows from the commit types since v0.3.0
No tag is created on a commit whose package.json version differs from the tag
The version bump goes through a branch and PR, not a direct commit to main
After merge, an annotated tag is pushed and gh release create --verify-tag is used
